paragraphs: On Saturday, the Explorers went to a campsite by a river. The bus left the school at half past seven. Teacher Kim sat at the front with a list of the children. The air was cool and fresh. At nine o'clock, the bus stopped at a green gate. The campsite had ten small tents and a long wooden hall. "Welcome, explorers," said Teacher Kim. "Today we walk, we look, and we listen."

First, the Explorers walked to the river. The river was brown, and a fast stream ran into it. The best place was on the other side, and the only way was a narrow bridge. The bridge was made of old wood, and it was above a fast stream. "The crossing is easy, but you must go one at a time," said Teacher Kim. Leo went first, and the bridge moved a little. "The bridge itself is old, but it is strong," said Teacher Kim. Then Mia went, and May and Lily went after her.

On the other side, they found a small wooden hut near the water. The hut was cool and quiet. Mia looked up at the ceiling and stopped. There was a nest on the ceiling, and two small birds sat in it. "Do not move," whispered Lily. A bird flew in with an insect, and the little birds opened their mouths. Mia took one photo, and she did not use the light of the camera. Her hands were very still. Lily wrote in her notebook: "A nest on the ceiling." Nobody spoke for a long minute.

At noon, they sat on the grass and ate lunch. A woman from the campsite gave each child a bowl of rice with vegetables. "Is that singing?" asked May. They listened, and they heard many birds in the trees. Then Leo started a song about a frog, and everybody joined in. The song was funny, and the woman from the campsite laughed too.

At three o'clock, the Explorers walked back over the bridge, and each child went carefully. The bus left the campsite at half past three. "You were good explorers today," said Teacher Kim. "You looked, you listened, and you waited." May slept on the bus, and Leo took a photo of her. Lily smiled and wrote a title for the blog: "The Nest on the Ceiling."
